Plot with Richard

```{r, echo=FALSE}
# Define the mapping of old column names to new labels

# Mapping special diets
diet_mapping <- c(
  "SpecialDiet_Toloseweight" = "To lose weight",
  "SpecialDiet_Togainweight" = "To gain weight",
  "SpecialDiet_Formedicalreasons" = "For medical reasons",
  "SpecialDiet_Glutenfree" = "Gluten free",
  "SpecialDiet_Wheatfree" = "Wheat free",
  "SpecialDiet_Dairyfree" = "Dairy free",
  "SpecialDiet_Vegetarian" = "Vegetarian",
  "SpecialDiet_Vegan" = "Vegan",
  "SpecialDiet_Notonaspecialdiet" = "Not on a special diet",
  "SpecialDiet_Other" = "Other"
)

# Reshape data
long_data <- survey_data %>%
  select(Q6_work_status, all_of(names(diet_mapping))) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = all_of(names(diet_mapping)), names_to = "SpecialDiet", values_to = "HasDiet") %>%
  filter(HasDiet == 1) %>%
  mutate(SpecialDiet = recode(SpecialDiet, !!!diet_mapping)) 

# Calculate percentages
long_data <- long_data %>%
  group_by(Q6_work_status, SpecialDiet) %>%
  summarise(Count = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(Q6_work_status) %>%
  mutate(Percentage = Count / sum(Count) * 100)

# Create interactive stacked bar chart
p <- ggplot(long_data, aes(x = as.factor(Q6_work_status), y = Percentage, fill = SpecialDiet, 
                           text = paste0(SpecialDiet, ": ", round(Percentage, 1), "%"))) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "stack") +
  labs(x = "Work Status", y = "Percentage", fill = "Special Diet",
       title = "Proportion of Special Diets by Work Status") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text")

```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
# Convert food security levels to factors

# Plot food security distribution
p1 <- ggplot(intake_data, aes(x = Combination1FoodSecurity)) +
  geom_bar(fill = "steelblue", color = "black") +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Food Security Levels",
       x = "Food Security Levels",
       y = "Count") +
  theme_classic()

ggplotly(p1)  # Convert to interactive
```

Here is the breakdown: 
0 --> Food secure
1-3 Moderate 
4-30 Low/Very Low

But the plot above is not right as each user has many inputs, so i need to aggreagate them by user




```{r}
# Extracting relevant columns
food_data <- intake_data[, c("Combination1FoodSecurity", "Fruit", "Driedfruit", "Fruitjuice", "Smoothiefruit", "Tomatoes")]

# Convert Combination1FoodSecurity to factor if not already
food_data$Combination1FoodSecurity <- as.factor(food_data$Combination1FoodSecurity)



# Plotting the comparison of food security levels with fruit consumption
ggplot(food_data, aes(x = Combination1FoodSecurity, y = Fruit, fill = Combination1FoodSecurity)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(title = "Food Security vs. Fruit Consumption",
       x = "Food Security Levels",
       y = "Fruit Consumption (units)") +
  theme_minimal()

# Repeat for other fruit/vegetable columns like Driedfruit, Fruitjuice, etc.
```

```{r}
# this is the latest code 

# Load necessary libraries
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(plotly)
library(stringr)  # For string manipulation

# Define a lookup table for work status descriptions
work_status_labels <- c(
  "2" = "Sick or Disabled",
  "3" = "Caring for Family",
  "4" = "Maternity/Paternity",
  "5" = "Other",
  "6" = "Prefer not to say",
  "7" = "Occupational Pension)",
  "8" = "State Pension)",
  "9" = "Student",
  "10" = "Unemployed long",
  "11" = "Unemployed short",
  "12" = "Work Full Time",
  "13" = "Work Part Time",
  "NA" = "Not Answered"
)

# Reshape the data from wide to long format
long_data <- survey_data %>%
  select(Q6_work_status, starts_with("Specialdiet_")) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("Specialdiet_"), names_to = "SpecialDiet", values_to = "Present") %>%
  filter(Present == 1) %>%
  mutate(SpecialDiet = str_remove(SpecialDiet, "^Specialdiet_")) %>%  # Remove prefix
  mutate(SpecialDiet = str_remove(SpecialDiet, "1$")) %>%  # Remove trailing '1'
  group_by(Q6_work_status, SpecialDiet) %>%
  summarise(Count = n(), .groups = 'drop') %>%
  mutate(Percentage = (Count / sum(Count) * 100))  # Convert counts to percentages within each work status

# Convert work status numbers to meaningful labels
long_data$Q6_work_status <- factor(long_data$Q6_work_status, levels = names(work_status_labels), labels = work_status_labels)

# Create the stacked bar chart with updated x-axis labels
# Create the filled bar chart
# Load necessary libraries
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(plotly)
library(stringr)  # For string manipulation

# Clean SpecialDiet labels
long_data <- long_data %>%
  mutate(SpecialDiet = str_remove(SpecialDiet, "^SpecialDiet_")) %>%  # Remove prefix
  mutate(SpecialDiet = str_replace_all(SpecialDiet, "_", " ")) %>%  # Replace underscores with spaces
  mutate(SpecialDiet = str_remove(SpecialDiet, "1$"))  # Remove trailing '1' if present

# Recode SpecialDiet labels for better readability

long_data <- long_data %>%
  mutate(SpecialDiet = recode(SpecialDiet,
    "For Medicalreasons" = "Medical Reasons",
    "To Gainweight" = "Gain Weight",
    "To Loseweight" = "Lose Weight",
    "Not On A Special Diet" = "No Diet"
  ))

# Create the filled proportional bar chart with cleaned legend labels
p <- ggplot(long_data, aes(x = Q6_work_status, y = Percentage, fill = SpecialDiet, 
                           text = paste0(SpecialDiet, ": ", round(Percentage, 1), "%"))) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "fill") +  # Use 'fill' instead of 'stack'
    labs(x = "Work Status", y = "Proportion", fill = "Special Diet",
         title = "Proportion of Special Diets by Work Status") +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format()) +  # Convert y-axis to percentage format
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 9))  # Adjust text size for readability

# Convert to an interactive plotly graph
ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text")


# Define work status labels
work_status_labels <- c(
  "2" = "Sick or Disabled",
  "3" = "Caring for Family",
  "4" = "Maternity/Paternity",
  "5" = "Other",
  "6" = "Prefer Not to Say",
  "7" = "Occupational Pension",
  "8" = "State Pension",
  "9" = "Student",
  "10" = "Unemployed Long",
  "11" = "Unemployed Short",
  "12" = "Work Full Time",
  "13" = "Work Part Time"
)

# Remove NA values from survey_data first
survey_data <- survey_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(Q6_work_status))

# Transform data
long_data <- survey_data %>%
  select(Q6_work_status, starts_with("Specialdiet_")) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("Specialdiet_"), names_to = "SpecialDiet", values_to = "Present") %>%
  filter(Present == 1) %>%  # Remove NA values from SpecialDiet
  mutate(SpecialDiet = str_remove(SpecialDiet, "^Specialdiet_"),  
         SpecialDiet = str_remove(SpecialDiet, "1$"),
         SpecialDiet = str_replace_all(SpecialDiet, "(?<=[a-z])([A-Z])", " \\1")) %>%  
  group_by(Q6_work_status, SpecialDiet) %>%
  summarise(Count = n(), .groups = 'drop') %>%
  group_by(Q6_work_status) %>%
  mutate(Percentage = (Count / sum(Count)) * 100) %>%
  mutate(SpecialDiet = str_remove(SpecialDiet, "^Special Diet_")) %>%  # Remove "Special Diet_" prefix
  mutate(SpecialDiet = str_replace_all(SpecialDiet, "_", " ")) %>%  # Replace underscores with spaces
  mutate(SpecialDiet = str_to_title(SpecialDiet)) %>%  # Capitalize words properly
  mutate(SpecialDiet = recode(SpecialDiet,
    "Notonaspecialdiet" = "No Preference",
    "Dairyfree" = "Dairy Free",
    "Formedicalreasons" = "Medical Reasons",
    "Glutenfree" = "Gluten Free",
    "Other" = "Other",
    "Togainweight" = "Gain Weight",
    "Toloseweight" = "Lose Weight",
    "Vegetarian" = "Vegetarian",
    "Wheatfree" = "Wheat Free",
    "Vegan" = "Vegan"
  ))
# Convert work status numbers to labels
long_data$Q6_work_status <- factor(long_data$Q6_work_status, levels = names(work_status_labels), labels = work_status_labels)




# Create the proportional bar chart
p <- ggplot(long_data, aes(x = Q6_work_status, y = Percentage, fill = SpecialDiet, 
                           text = paste0(SpecialDiet, ": ", round(Percentage, 1), "%"))) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "fill") +
    labs(x = "Work Status", y = "Proportion", fill = "Special Diet",
         title = "Proportion of Special Diets by Work Status") +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format()) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 9))

# Convert to an interactive plotly graph
ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text")


# put the bar chart into horizontal
p <- ggplot(long_data, aes(y = Q6_work_status, x = Percentage, fill = SpecialDiet, 
                           text = paste0(SpecialDiet, ": ", round(Percentage, 1), "%"))) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "fill") +  # Use 'fill' instead of 'stack'
    labs(y = "Work Status", x = "Proportion", fill = "Special Diet",
         title = "Proportion of Special Diets by Work Status") +
    scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format()) +  # Convert x-axis to percentages
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8))  # Adjust text size for readability

# Convert to an interactive plotly graph
ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text")
```
